routes.label: Check the circle condition

answerCheck.reason: Reflection symmetry gives QN=s, and the equal chords divide the upper semicircle into five 36° steps. Thus d=2cos36° and s=2sin18°=2cos72°. Consequently d²=2+s and s²=2-d, yielding d=(1+√5)/2 and s=(√5-1)/2. These give d-s=1, ds=1, and d²-s²=√5.

routes.label: Equal arcs and right triangles

answerCheck.reason: Number consecutive vertices V0 through V8 and let c be the chord spanning three sides. In cyclic quadrilateral V0V1V3V6, the sides are a, b, c, c and the diagonals are c, d. Ptolemy gives cd = ac + bc, so d = a + b.

routes.label: Split the longest diagonal using an equilateral triangle

answerCheck.reason: Let the fixed vertices have angles 40° and 60°. Equality of their distances to the moving vertex gives t=50° or 230°. Making either moving side equal to the fixed chord gives t=20° or 80° after excluding repeated vertices at 40° and 60°. Thus the sum is 20+50+80+230=380.

routes.label: Compare chords on the unit circle

answerCheck.reason: Extend BA beyond A to D with AD=AC=x. The equal arcs give ∠MAC=∠MAD, so SAS yields MD=MC=MB. Thus MP bisects DB, and PB=PD=AP+AD=(x+1)+x=2x+1.

routes.label: Extend the chord to build an isosceles triangle

answerCheck.reason: Let s,t be half the central angles for sides 3 and 5. Then s+t=60°, 2R sin s=3, and 2R sin t=5, giving R²=49/3. The dividing chord is 2R sin(3s)=9-27/R²=360/49, so m+n=409.

routes.label: Relate both trapezoids to their common radius

answerCheck.reason: Equal minor arcs AB and AC imply angle ACB = angle ABC = 70°. Thus angle BAC = 180° - 70° - 70° = 40°.

routes.label: Equal chords and an isosceles triangle

answerCheck.reason: The minor arcs AB and AC are each 150°, and AD is 120°. Equality DG = AB, together with BG > GA, forces arc AG = 30°, making GC a diameter. Right-triangle angle relations give AF/AB = tan15° = 2 - √3 and AE/AC = √3tan15° = 2√3 - 3. Their product is 7√3 - 12.

flags: Nondegenerate positions are understood. Collapsed chords or coincident angle rays require a limiting interpretation.

At C=A or C=B the chord collapses. At the perpendicular-diameter endpoint, the angle rays coincide. The ordinary angle-bisector argument applies to nondegenerate positions, with these exceptional positions interpreted by limits.

answerCheck.reason: Angles ACB and ADB subtend the same chord AB, so angle ACB = 40 degrees. Hence angle ABC = 180-70-40 = 70 degrees, equal to angle BAC. Their opposite sides satisfy AC = BC = 6.

routes.label: Equal arcs and cyclic quadrilateral equations

answerCheck.reason: Place the first chord's endpoints at clockwise angles 0° and 60°. The second chord crosses it when its starting angle lies in (0°,60°) or (300°,360°). These are two of six congruent arcs, so the probability is 2/6=1/3. Endpoint coincidences have probability zero.

answerCheck.reason: The scalene triangle has cyclic gaps of 1, 2, and 3 hexagon intervals. Its sides are 1, √3, and the diameter 2, so it is right and has area (1/2)·1·√3=√3/2.
